source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha, a.s. own annual reports (BCPP / PX Group as an issuer and as a market operator)
why_relevant: The exchange's own consolidated annual report is a quantified read on the health of the Czech listing channel itself: listing revenue, market-data revenue (market data licensing was 4.56% of PX Group operational revenue, CZK 35.057 million, with the latest fee change in 2025), member counts, IPO activity. Useful for judging whether the Prague issuer channel is expanding or shrinking as an intelligence surface. BCPP itself has an ISIN (CZ0008042603). Historical series of BCPP annual and quarterly reports sit on the ftp server (vz93–vz15, 1q15–3q16, BCPP_IFRS_2013/2014).

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Výroční zprávy (annual report PDFs, static path)
why_relevant: ČS annual reports are served as static PDFs on predictable /static_internet/ paths with a vz-YYYY.pdf filename convention, which sidesteps the JavaScript document app entirely for the single most important document per year. Note the directory segment has changed over time (older years sit under .../Obecne_informace/FSCS/...), so path templating must be per-era, not global.

source_name: Banka CREDITAS – emise dluhopisů (MREL) infoletters and prospectus programme
why_relevant: Challenger-bank corner of the cell, and a useful contrast case: CREDITAS funds MREL in CZK through the retail/domestic channel rather than EUR benchmarks. Retrieved facts include a CZK 1bn three-year MREL issue (CREDITAS 7,50/27, CZK 10,000 nominal, 7.5% fixed, maturity 30 July 2027, issuer call after two years, admitted to the Prague Stock Exchange regulated market), and a June 2024 prospectus permitting up to CZK 20bn of issuance with a first CZK 750m issue under a CZK 2bn programme. Small banks disclose funding cost and capital plans here that never appear elsewhere.

source_name: J&T Banka a Fio banka – komentáře k emisím MREL dluhopisů (broker research notes / zprávy z burzy)
why_relevant: Czech brokers publish short, dated notes on each domestic MREL/SNP issue, frequently ahead of or alongside the formal filing, and give pricing colour that issuers omit. Retrieved examples cover Banka CREDITAS MREL issues at 7.5% and MONETA's MREL programme — including a CZK 1.5bn issue at an 8% coupon, a mandate for a EUR 300m six-year non-call-five MREL bond at 4.41% p.a., nine-times oversubscription, bookrunners BNP Paribas and JPMorgan with Goldman Sachs Bank Europe and J&T Banka as co-managers, and the resulting +453bp move in MREL ratio to 28.23% against a 22.45% management target. That level of transaction detail is not in any prospectus.

source_name: RBI Country Sheet — Czech Republic (group network fact sheet)
why_relevant: A group-produced, one-country fact sheet — exactly the kind of artefact the local entity never publishes. Country sheets of this type typically carry business-volume, branch-count, employee-count, customer-count and market-position figures for the Czech market on a single comparable annual template, which makes cross-country and cross-year benchmarking cheap.

source_name: Fitch Ratings – Czech covered bond rating actions (e.g. Komerční banka soft bullet covered bonds)
why_relevant: Rating agency covered-bond commentary carries the analytics behind a programme — OC levels relied upon, D-Cap/discontinuity assessment, cover-pool credit assumptions, refinancing spreads — that neither the prospectus nor the HTT states as a judgement. KB's programme is rated AAA (Stable) by Fitch as of 24 June 2026; Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond was Moody's Aaa. Rating actions are also the most reliable public signal that a programme has changed materially.

source_name: PPF banka — document download tree (group bond prospectuses, Air Bank / Home Credit issuance docs)
why_relevant: PPF banka acts as arranger and paying agent for PPF-group bond issues (e.g. Air Bank CZK 1.5bn issue, PPF Financial Holdings CZK 4bn subordinated bonds, Home Credit B.V. CZK 1.998bn programme), so its document server hosts Czech-language prospectuses and terms for the whole group. Prospectuses contain business descriptions, risk factors and volume data with no equivalent elsewhere.

source_name: Société Générale — Universal Registration Document / Annual Financial Report (AMF filing)
why_relevant: The URD is the deepest single document on SG's Czech exposure: subsidiary list with ownership percentages for Komerční banka and its subsidiaries, the CRD Article 89 country-by-country annex (Czech Republic turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, FTE headcount), and risk/exposure tables by country. Filed annually with the AMF in March.

source_name: BNP Paribas — Universal Registration Document and Annual Financial Report
why_relevant: BNP Paribas no longer runs a Czech retail bank (Hello bank! by Cetelem closed CZ current/savings accounts in 2023 and transferred active loans to Česká spořitelna), but the group retains BNP Paribas Cardif pojišťovna, Arval CZ, Leasing Solutions, Securities Services and a CIB branch. The URD's consolidated-scope subsidiary table and country-by-country annex are the only place these Czech entities are enumerated with ownership and headcount in one document.

source_name: ECBC / EMF-ECBC – European Covered Bond Fact Book (Czech Republic chapter)
why_relevant: Annual reference work with a standing Czech Republic country chapter written by Czech market practitioners (a recent edition credits Pavel Kühn of Česká spořitelna). It sets out the legal basis — Act No. 190/2004 Coll. on Bonds as amended, and the Czech implementation of the EU Covered Bond Directive — the HZL definition, cover-pool eligibility, OC rules, outstanding volumes and issuer list. It is the fastest way to get an authoritative baseline of the Czech covered-bond framework and to date-stamp legal changes, without reading the statute.

source_name: PPF Financial Holdings a.s. — annual report (banking/consumer-finance sub-holding)
why_relevant: The intermediate holding that consolidates PPF banka, Air Bank, Home Credit CZ/SK, Yettel Bank and ClearBank. Its annual report is the closest thing to a 'Czech banking segment' disclosure for the PPF perimeter and is produced because the entity is a bond issuer, not because of listing obligations. Predecessor entity was PPF Financial Holdings B.V. — the a.s./B.V. redomiciliation matters for archive continuity.
